job.title: Intermediate Security Engineer, Security Incident Response Team (SIRT)

details.about: GitLab is a DevSecOps platform trusted by more than 50 million registered users to ship better, more secure software faster. Its Security Incident Response Team (SIRT), part of a globally distributed Security Operations group, is the front line protecting both GitLab.com and GitLab the company from security threats. This role works a compressed 4-day schedule (Sunday–Wednesday or Wednesday–Saturday) for 24/7/365 coverage and also supports GitLab's FedRAMP environment.
duties: Respond to and own security incidents in a 24/7 global rotation, from detection through containment and recovery
Create and maintain incident response documentation, including runbooks and standard procedures
Contribute to post-incident analysis through root cause analysis (RCA) and lessons-learned reviews
Build AI-assisted automation and tooling to improve efficiency and reduce manual work
Identify security gaps and help build advanced detection and response capabilities
Work across GitLab teams on new security capabilities and technical projects
needs: Demonstrated ability to learn and lead incident response processes independently
Experience with cloud platforms (GCP and/or AWS)
Experience building tools or automation with AI, and the judgment to test and verify what it produces
A proactive approach to identifying and investigating security threats
Interest in forensic analysis of infected hosts, and experience or a strong desire to learn cloud-based security investigations
United States citizenship and residency within the United States (government requirements)
details.benefits: United States base salary range $115,200 – $165,000 a year (bonuses, equity and benefits not included); level and salary are set through interviews and other factors. GitLab lists benefits for health, finances and well-being, flexible paid time off, team member resource groups, equity compensation and an employee stock purchase plan, a growth and development fund, and parental leave.
notes: Compressed 4-day work week: shifts run Sunday–Wednesday or Wednesday–Saturday
GitLab welcomes candidates who don't meet every single requirement
